**International Copper Study Group Environmental and Economic Committee Twenty Seventh Regular Meeting 6 October 2009, 10:45 a.m. – 1.00 p.m. Li** • **sbon, orP tugal ICSG Survey of Regulations Affecting Copper Products 2010 Edition** 

###### **ICSG/EEC/27/2** 

**1. The Survey.** This annual survey maps out national regulations, legislation and conventions affecting copper products in different countries and when possible, identifies copper the sectors, sub ‐ sectors and copper commodities and end use products containing copper potentially affected and in some cases the estimation of the impact. 

**2. Previous Regulatory Developments Covered.** In the October 2008 ICSG meeting, the secretariat provided members with an updated document with the changes in the regulatory environment for copper in 2008 (ICSG/EEC/25/4). The report surveyed changes in regulations affecting copper for the period between October 2007 to October 2008. The 2008 report identified international agreements related to climate change and expected impacts on energy generation and compliance costs. Also **p** resented advances in the desi **g** n of new EU ener **gy** and climate chan **g** e re **g** ulations, the im **p** lementation of chemical control legislation (REACH) and changes in the EU Drinking Water Directive. The 2008 survey also included United States Senate Bill 2006 restricting activities of scrap metal traders. Advances on the regulations for mining contract renegotiations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) where discussed. For China, the 2008 Survey included the decree raising China selling price of electricity, coke coal and aluminum new export tariffs in China, strengthened controls on inflows of foreign exchange, the Chinese import prohibition of copper related wastes, and the approved recycling law effective in 2009. Indonesia new mining legislation and smelting capacity impacts was included, same as law proposed to the Parliament in in Chile creating a ’ **Ministry of the Environment and an Environmental Enforcement Superintendent s Office** . **Advances of the draft for the new** mining law for Kazakhstan was included, same as new mining law and tax regime recently introduced in Zambia. The 2008 Western Australia’s new mine closure and rehabilitation system was summarized, followed by provincial legislation affecting copper/gold investments in Argentina, and advances in the new draft mining regulations in Ecuador. 

**3. Contents of ICSG Survey of Regulations 2009.** The survey starts with discussion of the current trade and economic env ronmen **i t th** a **t h** as **b** een **d** r v ng **i i** par **t** o **f th** e **2009** regu a **l ti** on presen **t** e **d** . **S** econ **dl** y we summar ze **i th** e **Chi** na **Sti** mu us **l** package and the copper related objectives of China Non Ferrous Metal Plan 2009 ‐ 2011. A summary of recent and coming trade and metal recycling regulations in China that affects the global copper markets.

A summary of the most recent, and most relevant to copper, changes in mining legislations ongoing around the world is discussed, followed by 2009 changes in regulations on energy legislation affectin the copper industry, including cap and trade and other greenhouse gas related regulatory advances and delays for key copper producer and user countries, inluding some air quality regulation update in **Canada affecting their copper smelters** . **The challenge for the copper industry** , **particularly for copper smelters with and** without H2SO4 plants of a recently signed United States mercury trade ban and the proposed UNEP Global Mercury Ban is discussed and some figures included. Finally, recent European regulatory trends are summarized, including the evolution of the EU Directive on Water Quality, the implementation and challenges of REACH registration for copper slag and the 13 copper intermediates by the copper consortium members is summarized, with advances of the EC on the implementation of REACH excluded copper ores in the Harmonic System UN ‐ GHS). Finally a summary of some of the WEEE Directive changes proposed by EU recyclers and the copper related outcoming EC proposal is discussed briefly.

#### **Senegal (West Africa) plan to reduce residential demand for electricity by . 20% with copper cable and energy efficient cu intensive home appliances** .
- **The national electrical safety council in Senegal (West Africa) has committed to an ECI coordinated project** that will reduce the residential demand for electricity by 20%. - This is a key objective, both in terms of energy efficiency and of taking some of the demand **pressure off an already stretched national capacity** . - ‐ - Fundamental to these efficiencies are new refrigerators and lamps for the home manufacturing partners for both are secured. - Discussions are now taking place with cable makers. Funding for the first phase of 1,250 homes is being sourced nationally and internationally, with funding for the rest of the country being facilitated by the Senegalese Government. - Over the past year, presentations on this concept have also been made to audiences around the world, both to raise awareness of the opportunity, as well as to identify other countries where this initiative could be replicated in 2010 and onwards. - Source: ECI (2009)
